findings.title: Cross-app domain leakage and weak bounded contexts
findings.snippet: OrderService.create_order(...) triggers notifications and payment side effects indirectly; PaymentService mutates Order/Inventory/Earnings.
findings.why: Core order, payment, analytics, and notification domains are tightly coupled via direct model/service calls, creating ripple effects and high change risk.
findings.consequence: Small payment-flow changes can break order/inventory logic, reducing release safety and team parallelism.
findings.refactor: Introduce domain events (OrderCreated, PaymentSettled, OrderDelivered) and asynchronous handlers; isolate write models per app boundary.
findings.example: Publish event in order app; subscribers in payment/analytics/notifications consume event with idempotency keys.
findings.impact: High: reduces regression blast radius and enables scale-out ownership.

findings.title: Fat API views containing orchestration/business rules
findings.snippet: APIView methods perform validation, querying, state transitions, and response shaping in one layer.
findings.why: Violates separation of concerns; hard to test deterministically; duplicates validation logic between views/services/serializers.
findings.consequence: Higher defect rate, inconsistent behavior across endpoints, expensive maintenance.
findings.refactor: Adopt use-case/application service layer + thin DRF views; serializers for I/O only, services for workflows.
findings.example: class CreateOrderUseCase.execute(command) -> DTO; view only maps request/response.
findings.impact: High: testability and maintainability improve materially.

findings.title: Multitenancy access model is inconsistent across apps
findings.snippet: queryset = Shop.objects.all(); queryset = Product.objects.all(); queryset = Inventory.objects.all()
findings.why: Object-level ownership filters are missing/uneven, while platform is multi-vendor.
findings.consequence: Cross-tenant reads/writes and data corruption risk.
findings.refactor: Introduce shared tenant-aware mixins/permissions and mandatory get_queryset ownership filters.
findings.impact: Critical: protects core data integrity and compliance.

findings.title: State machine rules distributed and partially duplicated
findings.snippet: Order status and payment status transitions are enforced in multiple places with partially overlapping checks.
findings.why: Transition invariants are not centralized in a single state machine.
findings.consequence: Impossible states and drift during feature additions (refund/cancel/deliver race paths).
findings.refactor: Create explicit transition policy module with allowed transitions + guard conditions and audit logging.
findings.impact: High: fewer lifecycle bugs in payments/orders.

findings.title: Potential N+1 and heavy in-memory aggregation in dashboards
findings.snippet: Looping through items/orders and computing totals in Python after broad queryset materialization.
findings.why: Loads large datasets into memory; repeated related-object accesses can explode query count under scale.
findings.consequence: Slow dashboards and higher DB/API latency at production volume.
findings.refactor: Push aggregation to DB using annotate/Sum/Case, paginate result sets, and precompute daily facts.

findings.title: Repository-level configuration drift and environment mismatch
findings.snippet: SQLite default in settings while platform context implies PostgreSQL production; requirements encoding malformed.
findings.why: Local/prod behavior diverges; tooling (linters/scanners) can fail on malformed dependency file.
findings.consequence: Hard-to-reproduce bugs and unstable CI/CD quality gates.
findings.refactor: Use env-driven DB config with explicit prod profiles; normalize requirements to UTF-8 and lock with hashes.

findings.title: Service naming and module layout inconsistency
findings.snippet: Misspelled app name `supliers`, generic file names (`service.py`), mixed conventions.
findings.why: Inconsistent naming impairs discoverability and onboarding.
findings.consequence: Higher cognitive load and accidental import mistakes.
findings.refactor: Rename modules to intent-revealing names (payout_service.py, order_checkout_service.py) and fix app naming.

findings.title: Transaction boundaries not uniformly aligned with side effects
findings.snippet: DB writes and external effects (payment gateway, notifications) can occur without outbox pattern.
findings.why: Failure between DB commit and external call causes inconsistent external/internal state.
findings.consequence: Ghost notifications, duplicate payouts, reconciliation mismatches.
findings.refactor: Use transactional outbox + worker processing for external IO; ensure idempotent consumers.
findings.example: Store outbox_event within atomic transaction, Celery worker dispatches reliably.

findings.title: Serializer responsibilities are mixed with domain defaults
findings.snippet: create() methods assign roles and defaults; validation duplicates model/business invariants.
findings.why: Domain rules in serializers complicate reuse outside HTTP and create hidden coupling.
findings.consequence: Inconsistent behavior in management commands, tests, and future async workflows.
findings.refactor: Move domain invariants to services/model methods; keep serializer for schema validation only.

findings.title: Insufficient pagination/filter standards across list endpoints
findings.snippet: Several list endpoints return full result sets without pagination controls.
findings.why: Unbounded responses increase DB load, memory, and network costs.
findings.consequence: Latency spikes and API instability under high cardinality datasets.
findings.refactor: Adopt global pagination policy + filter backends + max page size.
